# C8 — Structural claim boundaries

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **CONTRADICTED** — Current evidence contradicts the claim or one of its requirements. |
| Strongest accepted evidence | MODEL ONLY |
| Evidence classes cited | IMPLEMENTATION, TEST PROCEDURE, ANALYTICAL |
| Gate reached | SOFTWARE REPRODUCTION (next: SYNTHETIC TEST) |
| Last review | CURRENT — snapshot recorded 2026-09-28 by tooling snapshot (no human review) |

**Question.** Does the quasi-isotropic CFRP fin match or exceed aluminium stiffness, and does the Ti-6Al-4V hinge pin keep a factor of safety above 1.5?

**Current statement.** Classical laminate theory gives Ex = 56.68 GPa for the quasi-isotropic layup, below the 69 GPa aluminium comparison, so the stiffness claim is not met on modulus. A closed-form hinge-pin check gives a factor of safety of 1.88 against a 1.5 threshold. Neither is a physical test.

## Open questions

- The modulus result is below the comparison material (D-015); a thickness-compensation argument has not been calculated.

## Discrepancies

- [D-009](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-009) (OPEN) Model inputs were revised until paper targets were met
- [D-010](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-010) (OPEN) No shared design point across the mass, spring, reliability, and structural models
- [D-015](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-015) (OPEN) Laminate modulus is below the aluminium comparison

## Assumptions

- Handbook lamina properties, ideal layup, and the stated 50 g load case represent the design.

## Limitations

- Material modulus and component bending stiffness are different quantities.
- An analytical factor of safety is not a qualification test.
- Manufacturing defects and actual loads are unmeasured.
- The hinge load uses the 154 g fin whose mass conflicts with C4 (D-010).

## Measurement needed to close the next gate

- A component bending-stiffness calculation for equal-mass sections, reviewed.
- Coupon or component stiffness measurement if a CFRP fin is ever made.

## Pre-registered experiments

- None.

## What this claim does not establish

- Any inert physical measurement: none has been accepted for this claim.
- Physical performance of any hardware.
- Flight readiness or safety for live propulsion.
